name: main
proto: int main(int argc /*[bp+4]*/, char **argv /*[bp+6]*/, char **envp /*[bp+8]*/)  /* cdecl, called by crt0 at 1000:017e; NOT in Ghidra's function list */
purpose: The C main() of ULTIMA.EXE (Ghidra never created a function here; crt0 at 1000:017e pushes envp/argv/argc and `CALL 0`, then passes the return value to exit(02f4)). (1) Option letter: c = argc>1 ? to_upper(argv[1][0]) : ' '; sets the video-selection flags g_force_cga=(c=='C'), g_flag_herc=(c=='H'), g_flag_tandy=(c=='T'), g_flag_ega=(c=='E') (so `ULTIMA E` forces EGA). (2) g_error_hook = 1000:2322 (disk_error_hook); g_cur_disk=0; g_display_mode=0; g_floppy_count=1; d=get_current_drive_letter(); g_disk_drive_letters[0]=d; letter = (d>='C') ? d : 0xff is stored for disks 1,2 and 5 (0xa9c9/0xa9ca/0xa9cd), disk 3 (0xa9cb) = 0xff; g_ool_buffer_ptr (0xb11c) = 0xb21e; g_flush_after_key = 1. (3) INTRO_8b46() - the whole title/intro: sound on, identity g_tile_anim_map, detect_video_adapter, init_system, load_video_driver (retry loop), init_graphics_driver(1), colour setup, driver_init_screen (exit(1) on failure), load_font(0,IBM.CH)/load_font(1,RUNES.CH) (or .HCS on Hercules), the 'J'ourney-onward shortcut, title pictures, main menu (Journey/Create/Transfer/Use/Acknowledge/Return), and for Journey: draw_game_frame (637e), set_wind_and_draw(0), select_disk(3), load_file_region('SAVED.GAM', g_save_game, 0x1060, 0) and SAVED.OOL -> BRIT.OOL/UNDER.OOL, set_wind_and_draw(-1), g_cell_h=8; it returns only when a game is to be played. (4) draw_status_window(). (5) The location loop: quit=0; if g_location==0: MAINOUT_8ef2() (overworld main loop, returns when the party enters a settlement/dungeon or quits), quit=1, from_dungeon=0. If g_location is still 0 after that -> exit the loop (quit). Else if g_location < 0x21 (settlement): TOWN_93c0(quit||from_dungeon) (load the town; argument 1 = arriving from outside, clears monster slots) then TOWN_95ee() (town main loop), from_dungeon=0; else (dungeon 0x21..0x28): select_disk(2), DUNGEON_8ffe(quit), from_dungeon=1. quit=0. Then select_disk(1), spin until file_exists('BRIT.DAT'), load_file_region(OUTSUBS_a5f8() [= 'BRIT.OOL' if g_party_z==0 else 'UNDER.OOL'], g_monster_table, 0x100, 0) - reloads the overworld object list; if g_location==0 and g_party_z!=0 (Underworld): select_disk(5), wait for 'UNDER.DAT', save_file_region(OUTSUBS_a5f8(), g_monster_table, 0x100). Loop back to step 5 while quit==0. (6) restore_video_mode() and return (exit code AX).

0xb11c.name: g_ool_buffer_ptr
0xb11c.meaning: near pointer to the SAVED.OOL buffer (0xb21e)

0x5893.name: g_location
0x5893.meaning: 0 overworld, 1..0x20 settlement, 0x21..0x28 dungeon; selects which overlay main loop runs

0x5c5a.name: g_monster_table

notes: Bytes 1000:0000-017d. Startup chain: DOS entry 181d:0000 (PLINK stub) -> RETF to 172e:0322 (overlay-manager init: relocation delta into descriptor[0], preload overlays flagged 0x4000) -> JMPF 1000:017e (MSC crt0: DOS>=2 check, SS=DGROUP 0x1f64, SP=0xbd3e, shrink memory block (INT 21h/4Ah), zero BSS 0xa524..0xbd3f, INT 00h hook, FP init, argv/envp parsing) -> main -> exit. Note 0x5893 is named g_location here (part 1 called it g_input_mode because the intro stores '@'/'A' in it).

name: tile_transparent
proto: int tile_transparent(unsigned char tile /*param_2,[bp+6]*/, int dist_sq /*param_1,[bp+4]*/)
purpose: Line-of-sight helper used only by flood_visibility (5a28). Returns 1 if light/sight passes through `tile`. Tiles 'K' (0x4b), 'J' (0x4a), 0xba, 0xbb and 0x98 (windows / arrow slits / doors with windows) are transparent only when dist_sq == 1, i.e. when the cell is orthogonally adjacent to the viewer; every other tile is transparent unless it appears in the 19-byte opaque-tile list g_opaque_tiles (memchr(0x6a86, tile, 19) == NULL).

0x6a86.name: g_opaque_tiles
0x6a86.meaning: DATA.OVL file 0x6a96: tiles that block sight

notes: Call site in 5a28 passes (view_dist_sq, tile) in Ghidra order.

name: rebuild_light_map
purpose: Rebuilds g_light_map (0xad14, 32x32) for the current 32x32 map from the static light-source tiles. Fills the light map with 0xff, then scans rows y=0..31 / columns x=0..31 of the map via get_map_tile(g_chunk_x + x, g_chunk_y + y); every tile found in the 10-entry light-source list g_light_source_tiles (memchr(0x6a9a, tile, 10)) is written into g_light_map[y][x] and its (y,x) pushed on a local list (int[64] = max 32 sources; no overflow check). Then for each source: the 11x11 scratch area of g_view_tiles is filled with 0xff and flood_visibility(dest=g_light_map, stride=0x20, col_base=x-5, row_base=y-5, x0=x-5, y0=y-5, radius=10) floods the light outwards (cells with view_dist_sq <= 10 that the flood reaches get the tile value = lit). Finally every byte still 0xff becomes 0 (unlit). Called when a map is (re)loaded (TOWN_85d8, MAINOUT_81d0/8524), when a moongate appears (update_moongates), after combat (6150/6360), by CAST2 and SJOG.

0xad14.name: g_light_map
0xad14.meaning: 0 unlit, else lit (tile number); combat maps also live here

0x589b.name: g_chunk_x
0x589b.meaning: x of the cached map origin

0x589c.name: g_chunk_y
0x589c.meaning: y of the cached map origin

0x6a9a.name: g_light_source_tiles
0x6a9a.meaning: DATA.OVL file 0x6aaa: tiles that emit light (dc bd be b2 de bf b0 b1 b3 bc)

0xab02.name: g_view_tiles
0xab02.meaning: used as the flood's visited scratch grid here

notes: Light radius: flood radius 10 = squared distance, i.e. about 3 cells.

name: run_encounter
proto: void run_encounter(unsigned flags /*param_3,[bp+8]*/, int slot_or_watch /*param_2,[bp+6]*/, int camp_hours /*param_1,[bp+4]*/)
purpose: Common wrapper that runs one combat/camp scene inside the COMBAT overlay and restores the world afterwards. Saves g_party_x/y/z and g_active_member; g_combat_flags = flags; g_location_backup = g_location; g_location = 0xff (combat); copies the 0x100-byte monster table to g_monster_table_backup (0xa9fc). flags==0 (ordinary encounter with monster-table slot `slot`): type = 1 if (tile & 0xfc)==0x2c (pirate frigate) else (tile-0x40)>>2; if the slot's value1 >= 0x80 the type gets 0x100 OR'ed in (town 'group' marker, see setup_encounter); setup_encounter(1, type). flags&4 (camping, flags 4 outdoors / 6 in a dungeon): CMDS_bf80(flags, watch, hours) sets up the camp (party asleep except the watch, time passes); it returns 0 if nothing happened -> skip the fight. Otherwise flags&2 (dungeon room): DNGLOOK_b40e(0,2) places the party and the room's monsters. Any other nonzero flags skip straight to the cleanup. For a fight: g_active_member = 0xff, g_active_combatant = 0xff, g_no_more_enemies = 0 and COMBAT_ae24() (the combat main loop) runs. Cleanup: if g_tiles_patched (0xbb16) clear it and driver_tile_patch(1) (restore the two tile bitmaps DNGLOOK altered); g_location = backup; g_view_dirty = 1; restore x/y/z; draw_status_window(); g_active_member restored unless that member is now 'D' or 'S' (then 0xff); restore the monster table from the backup. Callers: fight_monster (6150), camp_outdoors (6360), hole_up_and_camp (flags 6), DUNGEON (rooms, flags 2, slot = g_monster_table[1].value1).

0x58a1.name: g_combat_flags
0x58a1.meaning: save 0x2FB: 0 encounter, 2 dungeon room, 4 outdoor camp, 6 dungeon camp

0x5894.name: g_location_backup
0x5894.meaning: save 0x2EE: location before combat (0xff is stored in g_location during combat)

0xa9fc.name: g_monster_table_backup
0xa9fc.meaning: copy of g_monster_table for the duration of combat (part 2 named slot 1 of it at 0xaa04)

0x58a3.name: g_no_more_enemies
0x58a3.meaning: save 0x2FD: set when all enemies are gone (Esc leaves combat); cleared here

0xbb16.name: g_tiles_patched
0xbb16.meaning: RAM: 1 when DNGLOOK applied driver_tile_patch(0); restored with command 1 after combat

0x5c5f.name: g_ship_hull
0x5c5f.meaning: slot value1: >= 0x80 marks a group encounter in towns

notes: Part 2's prose for hole_up_and_camp listed the arguments in Ghidra order; the true order is (flags, watch/slot, hours) as used by CMDS_bf80 ([bp+4]=hours added to g_hour).

name: load_combat_map
purpose: Loads combat map `index` (0..15) from BRIT.CBT: load_file_region('BRIT.CBT', g_light_map(0xad14), 0x160, index*0x160) - the 11 rows of 32 bytes land where the view code expects the combat map. Then copies the position tables out of the row tails: g_combat_party_x[6] (0x1724) <- 0xad7f (row 3, bytes 11..16), g_combat_party_y[6] (0x172c) <- 0xad85 (row 3, bytes 17..22), g_combat_monster_x[16] (0x1704) <- 0xaddf (row 6, bytes 11..26), g_combat_monster_y[16] (0x1714) <- 0xadff (row 7, bytes 11..26). ROOT always uses the row-3 party positions (the wiki's 'from south' set); DNGLOOK picks the row by entry direction for dungeon rooms.

0x1704.name: g_combat_monster_x
0x1704.meaning: monster start x per position index (DATA.OVL file 0x1714 holds defaults)

name: fight_monster
purpose:
Starts an encounter with monster-table slot `slot` (overworld/town). Prints '
' + centred creature name: 'PIRATES' if tile < 0x40, else g_monster_name_ptrs[(tile&0xfc - 0x40)/4] (DATA.OVL pointer table 0x18b6), then '

'. Chooses the combat map from the terrain under the monster (t = get_map_tile(x,y)) and the situation: water = t<4 or (t in 0x60..0x6f except bridges 0x6a/0x6b) or monster type tiles 0x80..0x8f (sea creatures). Special: type 0xfc (tiles 0xfc..0xff, the Shadowlord sprite group) -> map 10, and if g_sceptre (0x57b5) is set prints 'The Sceptre is reclaimed!', play_sweep_noise and clears it. Party on a frigate (g_transport_tile & 0xf8 == 0x20): pirates -> 14, water -> 11, else 13. On foot/horse/carpet: pirates -> 12, water -> 15, else by terrain: 8 -> 3; 1..3 -> 15; 4 -> 1; 5 -> 2; 6 -> 3; 7 -> 4; 0x1d -> 7; 9,0xa -> 5; 0xb..0xf -> 6; 0x1e,0x1f -> 4; 0x44 -> 8; 0x48,0x49 and 0x6a,0x6b -> 7; anything else -> 2 in the overworld, 8 in a settlement. Then load_combat_map(map); run_encounter(0, slot, 0); SJOG_dfbe(slot) (post-combat: ENDGAME if g_combat_exit=='M', restores the monster table, removes the defeated slot or turns a beaten pirate ship into a derelict frigate, prints '
', restores g_location); rebuild_light_map(); pass_time(0).

0x18b6.name: g_monster_name_ptrs
0x18b6.meaning: DATA.OVL file 0x18c6: pointers to the capitalised creature names

0x57b5.name: g_sceptre
0x57b5.meaning: save 0x20F: Sceptre of Lord British owned (0/0xff)

notes: Tile names are not in the reference files; the terrain->map mapping is given by tile number.

name: camp_outdoors
purpose: Overworld camping: load_combat_map(0), run_encounter(4, watch, hours) (CMDS_bf80 handles sleeping/healing/ambush; a fight runs only if it returns nonzero), then rebuild_light_map(). Called by hole_up_and_camp.

name: draw_game_frame
purpose: Draws the static main-screen frame once (called by INTRO when 'Journey Onward' starts). Clears the screen (colour 0, fill 0,0-319,199); in g_ui_color2 fills the bars: y0-6 full width, x0-6 and x185-191 for y0-191, y185-191 for x0-191, x313-319 for y0-87, y80-87 and y57-63 for x192-312. Sets text colour to g_ui_color2 and prints the ornament glyphs 0x7b at (col0,row0), 0x7c at (col39,row0), 0x7d at (col0,row23). In g_ui_color1 outlines: map view (7,7)-(184,184); a line x=191 from y191 up to 87 then to (319,87); status box (191,7)-(312,56); icon box (191,63)-(312,80). Finally set_text_color(g_ui_color1).
notes: All fill_rect/draw_line call sites are reversed (Pascal).

name: add_combatant
proto: int add_combatant(int type_or_member /*param_5,[bp+c]*/, int mode /*param_4,[bp+a]*/, u8 x /*param_3*/, u8 y /*param_2*/, u8 z /*param_1*/)
purpose: Adds an entry to the combat roster (0xba14, 8 bytes: +0 attack value, +1 initiative, +2 flags, +3 member/type, +4 monster-table slot, +5 turn counter, +6 x, +7 y) and a matching monster-table slot. mode 0 = monster of `type`: searches roster 6..31 for flags==0; +0 = g_monster_stats[type].hp? no - +0 = stats byte 4, +1 = stats byte 0 + rand_0_to(7) - 4 (if that exceeds 30 the raw stat is used), +5 = 36 - (+1), flags = 0x40 (monster) or 0x20 (inactive) for types 8 and 9, +3 = type, +6/+7 = x,y. mode 1 = party member `member` (roster 0..31, first free): if status != 'D': +1 = dexterity (record+0xd), +5 = 36 - dex, flags = 0x80 | (8 if status not 'G'/'P'); +3/+6/+7 set. Then the first monster-table slot with tile 0 is taken: mode 0 stores tile = anim = type*4+0x40 and value1 = stats byte 4 (HP); mode 1 stores value1 = member; both store x,y,z, value3(+7) = 0xff (no target) and the slot number in roster +4. mode 2 = bare object: no roster entry; tile = anim = type_or_member, value1 = type, result = the monster-table slot. Returns the roster index (mode 0/1), monster slot (mode 2) or -1 (0xffff) if no roster/monster slot was free. Finally, for every roster entry whose monster slot's value3 equals the new index, value3 is reset to 0xff (stale target). Callers: init_combat_party, setup_encounter, CAST/CAST2/COMSUBS/COMBAT (summons, clones: types 0x1f, 0x14, 0x26), DNGLOOK.

0xba14.name: g_combat_roster
0xba14.meaning: +0 attack(stat4) +1 initiative +2 flags +3 member/type +4 monster slot +5 turn counter (36-initiative) +6 x +7 y

0xba15.name: g_roster_initiative
0xba15.meaning: roster +1: dexterity for party members, stat0 +/-3 for monsters

0xba16.name: g_roster_flags
0xba16.meaning: 0x80 party, 0x40 monster, 0x20 inactive, 0x10 invisible, 0x08 asleep/incapacitated, 0x01 charmed

0xba18.name: g_roster_slot
0xba18.meaning: roster +4: monster-table slot of this combatant

0x13bd.name: g_monster_stats
0x13bd.meaning: DATA.OVL file 0x13cd: per creature type: +0 initiative base, +4 hit points, +5 max group size (8/0x10/1 = fixed), others unknown

0x5c61.name: g_monster_target
0x5c61.meaning: monster slot +7 during combat: roster index being targeted, 0xff none

notes: Which stat is which in g_monster_stats is inferred from use only (byte 4 copied into value1 = HP in combat, byte 0 -> initiative, byte 5 -> group size). Roster is RAM (not saved).

name: apply_ring_effects
purpose: For a party-side roster entry (flags & 0x80) that is neither inactive nor asleep (flags & 0x28 == 0): if the member's ring (record +0x1d) is item 42 '*' (Invisibility Ring) the combatant's monster-table anim tile (slot +1) becomes 0x1d (sprite 0x11d, the invisible marker) and roster flag 0x10 (invisible) is set; if it is item 44 ',' (Regeneration Ring) regeneration_ring_tick() is called (it takes no arguments - the pushed index is ignored and cleaned up by the caller's epilogue; it heals every ring wearer). Called per combatant by init_combat_party and each combat turn by SJOG_df92.

0xba16.name: g_roster_flags
0xba16.meaning: 0x80 party member, 0x20 inactive, 0x08 asleep, 0x10 invisible (set here)

0x5c5b.name: g_party_vehicle_tile
0x5c5b.meaning: monster slot +1 anim tile: 0x1d = invisible sprite

name: wake_combatant
purpose: Clears the asleep/incapacitated state (roster flag 8) of a combatant: for a monster the monster-table anim state (slot +6) is zeroed (animation resumes); for a party member the status becomes 'G' and the anim tile is restored to the base tile (slot +0), or to 0x1d if the invisible flag 0x10 is set. Flag 8 is cleared and draw_status_window() is called in all cases. Used by CAST (An Zu / awaken), CMDS (end of camping), COMBAT.

name: sleep_combatant_unless_poisoned
purpose: Calls incapacitate_combatant(index) unless the entry is a party member whose status is 'P' (poisoned members cannot fall asleep). Used by CMDS_bf80 when camping to put everyone except the watch to sleep.

name: incapacitate_combatant
purpose: Puts a combatant to sleep. Monster: roster flag 8 set, g_combat_state_flags = 4, monster-table anim state (slot +6) = 0xff (frozen). Party member: return if dead; status = 'S', flag 8 set, anim tile = 0x1e (sprite 0x11e, sleeping body); if this was g_active_member it becomes 0xff; g_combat_state_flags = 4; draw_status_window(); if camping (g_combat_flags & 4) return without redrawing. Otherwise refresh_map_view(). Callers: CAST (sleep spells), COMBAT, SJOG, init_combat_party (members already 'S'), sleep_combatant_unless_poisoned.

0x58a2.name: g_combat_state_flags
0x58a2.meaning: save 0x2FC: set to 4 whenever a combatant falls asleep (COMBAT also uses bits 1, 0x20); exact meaning not determined

0x587b.name: g_active_member
0x587b.meaning: cleared if the sleeper was active

name: init_combat_party
purpose: Prepares the roster and monster table for a fight. Zeroes bytes +0..+6 of all 32 monster-table slots (value3/+7 is NOT cleared) and all 8 bytes of the 32 roster entries. For each living party member i (< g_party_count, status != 'D'): if the ring is 42 or 44, with probability 1/16 (rand_range(0,15)==11) prints 'A ring has vanished!', play_tone_sweep(1200,2000,1,40) and remove_equipped_item(i, ring). Then r = add_combatant(i, 1, g_combat_party_x[i], g_combat_party_y[i], g_party_z); the member's monster slot gets target 0xff and a sprite by class (record +0xa): 'A' -> 0x4c, 'B'/'S'/'T' -> 0x44, 'D'/'M' -> 0x40, 'F'/'P'/'R' -> 0x48 (0x100-relative; the default from add_combatant is kept for other classes); anim tile = tile; then incapacitate_combatant(r) if the member is 'S', else apply_ring_effects(r). Finally if the centre cell of the combat map (g_light_map[5][5], 0xadb9) is 0xdc, add_combatant(1, 2, 5, 5, z) creates a bare object of type 1 (sprite 0x101, presumably a chest) there with value1 = 3*z + 7 and the centre cell is replaced by g_dungeon_floor_tile (0xbb15).

0xbb15.name: g_dungeon_floor_tile
0xbb15.meaning: RAM: floor tile of the current dungeon style (0x45 or 5), set by DUNGEON_8ffe

0x5895.name: g_party_z
0x5895.meaning: z for all combatants and the chest value

notes: The 0xdc centre-object rule and 'chest' identification are inferred; the sprite numbers are the usual 0x100-relative monster-table values.

name: setup_encounter
purpose: Populates a fight with monsters of creature `type`. Bit 0x100 of type is a 'forced group' marker (set by run_encounter when the slot's value1 >= 0x80) and is stripped. g_combat_exit = 0. Unless flags & 4 (camping, which already built the party) init_combat_party(). A 16-entry position permutation is the identity, or shuffled when camping (for each i: swap with rand_range(0,15)). Prints '*** CONFLICT ***\n'. Group size: if the pre-combat location is the overworld or a dungeon, or type == 12, or the group marker was set, n = g_monster_stats[type].group (+5); in a settlement otherwise n = 1. Unless n is 8, 16 or 1 (fixed sizes) n = rand_range(1,n), rolled a second time (rand_range(1,n)) when g_unk_5959 != 0; refresh_map_view(); n capped at 26. First monster: add_combatant(type, 0, g_combat_monster_x[p[0]], g_combat_monster_y[p[0]], z). For i = 1..n-1: t = type, but for i <= n/4 with probability 1/9 (rand_0_to(8)==0) t = g_monster_alt_type[type] (0x16d4, a companion creature); add_combatant(t, 0, x[p[i]], y[p[i]], z). The permutation has only 16 entries, so monsters 17..26 index past it into other locals (garbage positions) - reproduce or guard deliberately.

0x58a0.name: g_combat_exit
0x58a0.meaning: save 0x2FA: exit direction/outcome of combat (0 none, 1-6 W/E/N/S/U/D, 'M' triggers ENDGAME)

0x16d4.name: g_monster_alt_type
0x16d4.meaning: DATA.OVL file 0x16e4: companion creature type spawned with 1/9 chance among the first quarter of a group

0x5959.name: g_unk_5959
0x5959.meaning: save 0x3B3: nonzero halves encounter sizes (second rand roll); reset monthly by pass_time

notes: Callers: run_encounter (flags=1) and CMDS_bf80 (ambush while camping, flags=g_combat_flags).

name: combat_pos_in_bounds
purpose: Returns 1 if 0 <= x <= 10 and 0 <= y <= 10 (inside the 11x11 combat map), else 0. Used by CMDS (movement) and COMBAT (ranged targeting).

name: compute_member_defense
purpose: Ghidra dropped most of this function as 'unreachable'; the assembly is: if the pre-combat location is 0x28 (dungeon Doom) and the member's armour (record +0x1a) is not item 15 (Mystic Armour) return 0. Otherwise sum g_item_defense[item] (DATA.OVL 0x1634, 'armour and weapon defensive values') over the six equipment slots helmet +0x19, armour +0x1a, left hand +0x1b, right hand +0x1c, ring +0x1d, amulet +0x1e, skipping empty slots (0xff); add 3 while the status icon is 'P' (Protection spell). Returns the total defence value.

0x1634.name: g_item_defense
0x1634.meaning: DATA.OVL file 0x1644: defensive value per item id

0x55c1.name: g_party_helmet
0x55c1.meaning: record +0x19 (0x55c2 armour, 0x55c3 left hand, 0x55c4 right hand, 0x55c5 ring, 0x55c6 amulet)

notes: Decompiled text is wrong (shows only the Doom check and a bogus 'return 3'); use the listing at 1000:6da8-6e5f.

name: remove_equipped_item
purpose: Unequips `item` from the member's record: checks helmet (+0x19), armour, left hand, right hand (+0x1c), then ring (+0x1d), then amulet (+0x1e) in that order and sets the first matching slot to 0xff. Special case for the ring slot: if the item is 42 (Invisibility Ring) and we are in combat (g_location >= 0x80) with g_active_combatant < 32, roster flag 0x10 (invisible) of the active combatant is cleared. Returns 1 if the item was found in some slot, 0 otherwise. Always ends by calling compute_member_defense(member) whose result is discarded. Callers: init_combat_party (vanishing ring), COMBAT (glass sword 39 breaks), SJOG (chaos sword 35), COMSUBS (flaming oil 19 thrown), ZSTATS (remove command).

name: str_find_ci
purpose: Case-insensitive substring search (assembly). Computes both lengths with str_len_es (6f90) into g_strfind_needle_len (0x6aa4) and g_strfind_limit (0x6aa6) = len(hay) - len(needle); returns -1 (0xffff) if the needle is longer. Compares characters with bit 7 stripped and letters > 0x60 folded to upper case (AND 0x5f). On a full match returns the offset of the match in the haystack. On a mismatch after k matched characters it advances by k+1 (not by 1), so some overlapping matches are missed - keep this behaviour. Used by TALK (keyword matching of typed input), CMDS/CAST2 (spell syllables, command words), LOOKOBJ, SHOPPES2.

0x6aa6.name: g_strfind_limit
0x6aa6.meaning: RAM scratch: last start offset to try

notes: Ghidra's pointer-arithmetic rendering is misleading; see listing 6f1e-6f8d.

name: str_len_es
proto: /* ES:DI = string */ str_len_es() -> DI = length (bytes before NUL); clobbers AL,CX,BX
purpose: Register-called strlen helper for str_find_ci: REPNE SCASB for a NUL over up to 0xffff bytes and returns the length in DI.
notes: Not Pascal; only used by 6f1e.

name: driver_tile_patch_special
proto: void driver_tile_patch_special(int n /*param_1,[bp+4]*/)  /* pascal: AX = n+3 */
purpose: Calls driver entry 36 (offset 0x6c) with AX = n+3, i.e. tile-set patch command 3 (n=0, from DNGLOOK_b3c0) or 4 (n=1, from ENDGAME_a8d8). In EGA.DRV command 3 swaps the two middle bytes of every 4-byte group in the bitmaps of tiles 5, 0x1e, 0x1f, 0x4c, 0xca, 0x20-0x26, 0x30-0x37 and 0x60-0x6f (a plane/colour swap of those tiles - a visual effect, exact look not determined); command 4 is a further variant (at EGA.DRV 0x2c4e, not examined). Ghidra mis-decompiled the body (it shows a call through a string); the listing bytes are MOV AX,[BP+4]; ADD AX,3; MOV [5350],0x6c; CALLF [5350]; RET 2.
notes: Tile-set offsets in the driver: tile t at t*0x80 in the segment stored at EGA.DRV cs:0x206.

name: driver_tile_patch
proto: void driver_tile_patch(int cmd /*param_1,[bp+4]*/)  /* pascal: AX = cmd */
purpose: Driver entry 36 with AX = cmd. cmd 0 (DNGLOOK_aefc, when it also sets g_tiles_patched=1): the driver saves 8 bytes of tile bitmap at tile-set offsets 0x6470 (row 14 of tile 0xc8) and 0x8bf0 (row 14 of tile 0x117) into its own buffer and overwrites each with the tile's row 0 (offset -0x70). cmd 1 (run_encounter after combat, when g_tiles_patched): restores the saved bytes. Net effect: temporarily alters two tile images while inside certain dungeon rooms. cmd 2 is driver_set_clock_tile (71aa); 3/4 see 6f9e.
notes: Which images tiles 0xc8 / 0x117 are is not confirmed (0x117 is drawn for ladders by place_object_in_view).

name: driver_animate_tile_bitmaps
purpose: Calls driver entry 32 (offset 0x60) with the carry flag clear and AX = g_font_segs[0] (the IBM.CH font segment; the CF=1 path of the same entry is draw_effect_frame). In EGA.DRV the CF=0 path mutates the tile bitmaps in place each frame: 32 iterations write a pseudo-random byte (same LCG as rand_range, private seed in the driver) into 9 positions of each 4-byte group of the four tiles at tile-set offset 0xf400 (tiles 0x1e8-0x1eb, i.e. sprites 0xe8-0xeb - fire/flame-like sprites), then rotates the rows of the tile at offset 0x80 (tile 1, deep water) by one row (block moves of 0x3c words) and continues with further tiles (offset 0x100...). Called once per animation frame by animate_monsters after cycle_tile_anim_map; it is the 'noise and scroll' half of the terrain animation and consumes the driver's RNG, not g_rand_seed.

0x539c.name: g_font_segs
0x539c.meaning: [0] passed in AX (apparently unused by the EGA driver)

notes: For the port: implement as a per-frame mutation of the water and fire tile images; exact pixel pattern only matters cosmetically.

name: view_dist_sq
purpose: Squared distance of view cell (a,b) from the view centre (5,5) via the quadrant table: if either coordinate >= 11 returns 0; coordinates > 5 are mirrored (10-v); returns g_view_dist_sq[b][a] (DATA.OVL 0x6aa8, 6x6 bytes, x*x+y*y). Symmetric, so argument order does not matter. Used by flood_visibility (light radius / adjacency test) and place_objects_in_view (desert tile swap).

name: draw_light_beam_frame
proto: void draw_light_beam_frame(int frame /*param_4,[bp+a]*/, int on /*param_3,[bp+8]*/, int x /*param_2,[bp+6]*/, int y /*param_1,[bp+4]*/)
purpose: Writes one orientation of the rotating light beam into the town light map: for the 16 (dx,dy) signed byte pairs of pattern row (frame % 16) in g_light_beam_pattern (0x1f7e, 16 rows x 32 bytes) sets g_light_map[(y+dy)*32 + x+dx] to 0xff when on==1, else 0. No bounds checks (row wrap-around is possible near map edges; the source sits well inside the map). 0xff counts as 'lit' for the visibility flood.

0x1f7e.name: g_light_beam_pattern
0x1f7e.meaning: DATA.OVL file 0x1f8e: 16 beam orientations x 16 relative cells (dx,dy); unused pairs are (0,0)

notes: The wiki marks file 0x1f7e-0x21da as unknown; the first 16 bytes before the pattern are the shrine x/y lists.

name: animate_light_beam
purpose: Per-frame rotating light beam (lighthouse style) in settlements; called by refresh_map_view outside combat. If g_light_level >= 0x32 (full daylight) or there is no beam source (g_beam1_x == -1): g_beam_frame = 0xff (idle) and return. Otherwise g_view_dirty = 1 and: if the frame is 0xff, start: frame = 0 and draw frames 0,1,2 ON at source 1 (0x217e/0x2180) and, if g_beam2_x != -1, at source 2 (0x2182/0x2184); else erase frame f at both sources, f++, draw frame f+2 at both. Frames wrap 16 -> 0 (the pattern index is taken mod 16 anyway). So three adjacent orientations are lit at a time and the beam sweeps one step per map refresh. Sources are set by TOWN_85d8 (first two '*' (0x2a) tiles found in the town map, -1 if none) and OUTSUBS (the 0x1b tile in the cached overworld chunks).

0x217e.name: g_beam1_x
0x217e.meaning: RAM-ish in DATA.OVL (file 0x218e): x of light source 1, -1 none

0x24e6.name: g_view_dirty
0x24e6.meaning: set every frame while the beam runs

notes: Identification as the lighthouse beam is inferred from the rotating 16-orientation pattern and night-only gating; tile names 0x2a/0x1b are not in the references.

name: driver_set_clock_tile
purpose: Driver entry 36 command 2: passes the game hour and minute so the driver redraws the hands of the clock tile (tile-set offset 0x7d10 = tile 0xfa) in place. Called by pass_time whenever time advances in a settlement, so the clocks seen in towns show the game time.
notes: Ghidra shows a bogus call through a string; see listing 71aa-71c9.

name: scroll_rect_up
proto: void scroll_rect_up(int x1 /*[bp+c] AX*/, int y1 /*[bp+a] BX*/, int x2 /*[bp+8] CX*/, int y2 /*[bp+6] DX*/, int rows /*[bp+4] SI*/)
purpose: normalize_rect (08e6) on the four coordinates, clamps rows to (y2-y1), negates it and calls driver entry 13 (offset 0x27, the window-scroll routine also used by put_char) with SI = -rows: scrolls the rectangle's pixels up by `rows` pixel rows. Used by earthquake_shake.

name: scroll_rect_down
proto: void scroll_rect_down(int x1 /*[bp+c]*/, int y1 /*[bp+a]*/, int x2 /*[bp+8]*/, int y2 /*[bp+6]*/, int rows /*[bp+4]*/)
purpose: Same as scroll_rect_up but passes SI = +min(rows, y2-y1) to driver entry 13: scrolls the rectangle down. Used by earthquake_shake.

name: dos_read_region
proto: unsigned dos_read_region(const char *name /*[bp+a]*/, void *buf /*[bp+8]*/, unsigned count /*[bp+6]*/, unsigned offset /*[bp+4]*/)
purpose: Assembly DOS wrapper used by load_file_region (256e): g_last_dos_error = 0; INT 21h/3Dh open (AL=2 read/write); if the open fails or the INT 24h handler flagged an error (g_last_dos_error != 0) -> error; if offset != 0, INT 21h/42h lseek to CX:DX = 0:offset (16-bit offsets only, enough for the 0x1060-byte save and 0x400-byte map pages); count 0 means 0xffff; INT 21h/3Fh read into DS:buf; INT 21h/3Eh close. Returns the number of bytes read; on any failure stores the DOS error code in g_last_dos_error, calls the far error hook g_error_hook and returns 0 (load_file_region then retries).
notes: RET 8.

name: dos_write_file
proto: unsigned dos_write_file(const char *name /*[bp+8]*/, const void *buf /*[bp+6]*/, unsigned count /*[bp+4]*/)
purpose: Assembly DOS wrapper used by save_file_region (25d8): INT 21h/3Ch create/truncate (attributes 0), INT 21h/40h write count bytes from DS:buf, INT 21h/3Eh close (flags preserved around the close). Success: g_last_dos_error = 0, returns bytes written. Failure of create or write: g_last_dos_error = DOS code, calls g_error_hook, returns 0.
notes: RET 6. Last function of ROOT; 72d5-72df padding.
